claim: Patiria miniata larvae have an extensive nervous system at 7 days post fertilization (7dpf).
source: Sea star bipinnaria larvae have an extensive nervous system (Katow et al., 2009; Murabe et al., 2008; Nakajima et al., 2004; Carter et al., 2021; Elia et al., 2009; Hinman and Burke, 2018). Figure 1A–B'' shows the 7-day post fertilization (7dpf) P. miniata larval nervous system labeled via localization of anti-synaptotagmin B (SynB) and serotonin antibodies.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature and immunostaining data shown in Figure 1A-B''

claim: Anti-synaptotagmin B (SynB) labels all neurons in many echinoderm species.
source: It has been shown that the pan-neuronal marker SynB labels all neurons in many echinoderm species (Burke et al., 2006; Nakajima et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: Serotonin immunoreactivity is concentrated predominantly in the anterior part of P. miniata larvae, in the dorsal ganglia with a subset of cells across the aboral surface.
source: Serotonin immunoreactivity is concentrated predominantly in the anterior part of the larvae; in the dorsal ganglia with a subset of cells across the aboral surface (Figure 1B, D' and E').
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B, D', and E'

claim: Bisection of P. miniata larvae removes the anterior serotonergic neurons.
source: Indeed, when we bisect the larvae across the midline, 40 of 45 stained larvae show no remaining serotonergic neurons 1 day later, when they were first assayed. Figure 1F'–f shows one such example. Of the remaining five, only one or two cells were found which, due to their location, are likely those normally associated with the lower lip of the mouth.
evidence: Supported by quantitative data from immunostaining experiments and shown in Figure 1F'-f

claim: Serotonergic neurons are first detected at the anterior regenerating leading edge in 8/14 larvae 5 days following bisection.
source: By examining a time series of regeneration, we show that serotonergic neurons are first revealed by antibody staining at the anterior regenerating leading edge in 8/14 larvae 5 days following bisection (Figure 1G'–g).
evidence: Supported by quantitative immunostaining data shown in Figure 1G'-g

claim: By 7 days post bisection (dpb), serotonergic neurons are found in 12/15 regenerating larvae at the anterior edge.
source: By 7 days post bisection (dpb), serotonergic neurons are found in 12/15 regenerating larvae at the anterior edge (Figure 1H'–h).
evidence: Supported by quantitative immunostaining data shown in Figure 1H'-h

claim: Three weeks following bisection, the regenerated serotonergic neurons are bilaterally patterned at the dorsal side of the regenerating larvae, resembling the dorsal ganglia structure found in intact larvae.
source: Three weeks following bisection, the regenerated serotonergic neurons are bilaterally patterned at the dorsal side of the regenerating larvae, resembling the dorsal ganglia structure found in intact larvae (Figure 1I'–i).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1I'-i

claim: The anterior serotonergic neurons are removed following anterior bisection and are reformed in the correct general location and with extensive axonal projections by 21 days of regeneration.
source: These data therefore show that the anterior serotonergic neurons are removed following anterior bisection and are reformed in the correct general location and with extensive axonal projections by 21 days of regeneration.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the immunostaining time series data presented in Figure 1

claim: During normal embryogenesis, sox2 is expressed broadly throughout the neurogenic ectoderm.
source: We have shown that, during normal embryogenesis, the SRY-box TF, sox2, (formerly soxb1) is expressed broadly throughout the neurogenic ectoderm (Yankura et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Serotonergic neurons form from cells expressing sox4 that are first present and distributed in a 'salt and pepper' pattern throughout the ectoderm of the embryonic blastula.
source: Serotonergic neurons form from cells expressing the SRY-box TF, sox4 (formerly soxc) that are first present and distributed in a 'salt and pepper' pattern throughout the ectoderm of the embryonic blastula (Yankura et al., 2013; Yankura et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Foxq2 and six3 are expressed in the anterior ectoderm of the early gastrula and are required for the correct progression of the anteriorly most located sox4+ neural progenitors to become lhx2+ cells.
source: Two transcription factors, foxq2 and six3, are expressed in the anterior ectoderm of the early gastrula and are required for the correct progression of the anteriorly most located sox4+ neural progenitors to become lhx2+ cells.
evidence: Supported by reference to embryonic neurogenesis pathway shown in Figure 2A-C

claim: After asymmetric cell divisions, lhx2+ progenitors give rise to post-mitotic neurons expressing elav.
source: After asymmetric cell divisions, lhx2+ progenitors in turn give rise to post-mitotic neurons expressing elav (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by the embryonic neurogenesis pathway diagram in Figure 2A-C

claim: Post-mitotic neurons expressing elav produce serotonin when they mature.
source: These post-mitotic neurons will produce serotonin when they mature (Cheatle Jarvela et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Foxq2 and six3 are re-expressed in the anterior ectoderm of the leading regenerating edge by 3dpb.
source: Following bisection, we find that foxq2 and six3 are expressed in the anterior ectoderm of the leading regenerating edge by 3dpb (Figure 2D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-H).
evidence: Supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-H

claim: Foxq2 is expressed in cells that, in the normal larvae, reside along the middle of the AP axis and would never normally express anterior markers such as foxq2.
source: It is important to note therefore, that foxq2 is now expressed in cells that, in the normal larvae, reside along the middle of the AP axis and would never normally express anterior markers such as foxq2.
evidence: Inference based on the spatial location of foxq2 expression in regenerating larvae compared to normal development

claim: The anterior leading edge cells are being respecified during regeneration, at least partially recapitulating the embryonic axial state required for neurogenesis.
source: This indicates that the anterior leading edge cells are being respecified, as defined by expressing new sets of genes, during regeneration. This respecification, at least partially, recapitulates the embryonic axial state required for neurogenesis.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from gene expression data showing re-expression of embryonic axial markers

claim: Sox2 expression is dramatically up-regulated at the wound site within 1 day following bisection.
source: Sox2 is expressed at low levels throughout the ectoderm of the normal larvae (Yankura et al., 2013; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) but within 1 day following bisection, sox2 expression is dramatically up-regulated at the wound site (Figure 2E–e, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), when compared to larval expression levels.
evidence: Supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2E-e and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B

claim: Localized sox2 expression precedes the formation of the proliferative zone but then remains within the anterior region.
source: We have previously shown that cell division occurs throughout the normal larva, but then decreases in the early bisected larva and is then predominantly localized to the wound adjacent anterior at 3dpb (Cary et al., 2019b). Thus, localized sox2 expression precedes the formation of the proliferative zone but then remains within this anterior region.
evidence: Inference based on comparison of sox2 expression timing with previously published cell division data

claim: Sox2 is highly expressed throughout the ectodermal proliferative zone and within some proliferating cells at 3dpb.
source: This costaining shows that sox2 is highly expressed throughout this ectodermal zone and within some of these proliferating cells at 3dpb (Figure 2F–f, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C) and that this remains through to 5dpb (Figure 2G–g, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Supported by EdU-FISH data shown in Figure 2F-f and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-D

claim: Sox4 expression is observed at the wound site within one day following bisection.
source: Sox4 expression, a marker of neural precursor cells, is also observed at the wound site within one day following bisection (Figure 2H–h', and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: Supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2H-h' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F

claim: Sox4+ cells undergo cell divisions as FISH staining colocalizes with EdU.
source: Thus we show that sox4+ cells clearly undergo cell divisions as FISH staining colocalizes with EdU (Figure 2I–i').
evidence: Supported by EdU-FISH data shown in Figure 2I-i' with 3D visualization

claim: By 5dpb, sox4 expression is concentrated to the regenerating anterior, in dividing cells.
source: By 5dpb, sox4 expression is concentrated to the regenerating anterior, again in dividing cells (Figure 2J–j', and Figure 2—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: Supported by EdU-FISH data shown in Figure 2J-j' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2H

claim: The expression of lhx2 is detected by 5-7dpb in dispersed cells at the regenerating leading edge.
source: The expression of lhx2 is also detected by 5-7dpb in dispersed cells at the regenerating leading edge (Figure 2 K-K2, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2J).
evidence: Supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2K-K2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2J

claim: The expression of post-mitotic neural marker elav is restored at the regenerating anterior at 5-7dpb.
source: Similarly, the expression of post-mitotic neural marker elav is also restored at the regenerating anterior at 5-7dpb (Figure 2L–l', and Figure 2—figure supplement 2L).
evidence: Supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2L-l' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2L

claim: Sox4/lhx2 co-expression is found in cells located at the lateral sides of the regeneration leading edge.
source: Two-color FISH shows that, similar to embryogenesis, sox4/lhx2 co-expression is found in cells located at the lateral sides of the regeneration leading edge (Figure 2K–l')
evidence: Supported by two-color FISH data shown in Figure 2K-l'

claim: Lhx2 and elav are co-expressed in regenerating larvae.
source: and that lhx2 and elav are also co-expressed.
evidence: Supported by two-color FISH data shown in Figure 2L-l'

claim: Bisection leads to the activation of embryonic neurogenesis gene expression states.
source: Collectively, these data show that bisection leads to the activation of embryonic neurogenesis gene expression states.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the gene expression data showing sequential expression of sox2, sox4, lhx2, and elav

claim: Sox2 and sox4 expressions are induced upon wounding, and sox4+ cells located at the lateral leading edge give rise to lhx2+ cells.
source: Sox2 and sox4 expressions are induced upon wounding, and sox4+ cells located at the lateral leading edge give rise to lhx2+ cells.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the sequential gene expression and colocalization data

claim: The lhx2+ cells at the leading edge become post-mitotic neurons expressing elav.
source: The lhx2+ cells at the leading edge in turn become post-mitotic neurons expressing elav (Figure 2M).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from colocalization data and shown in model in Figure 2M

claim: The location of lhx2 expression at the leading edge, within the zone of foxq2 expression, recapitulates the spatial localization of embryonic serotonergic cell specification.
source: The location of lhx2 expression at the leading edge, within the zone of foxq2 expression, also recapitulates the spatial localization of embryonic serotonergic cell specification.
evidence: Inference based on comparison of spatial gene expression patterns between regeneration and embryonic development

claim: The sox4:GFP recombinant BAC faithfully expresses GFP in sox4+ cells, recapitulating endogenous sox4 expression.
source: When the sox4:GFP recombinant BAC is injected into embryos, it faithfully expresses GFP in sox4+ cells, recapitulating endogenous sox4 expression (Cheatle Jarvela et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: The approximately 150 Kbp surrounding the genomic locus of the sox4 coding region, including the endogenous basal promoter, is sufficient to drive correct expression of the transgenic GFP reporter gene.
source: This demonstrates that the approximately 150 Kbp surrounding the genomic locus of the sox4 coding region, including the endogenous basal promoter, is sufficient to drive correct expression of the transgenic GFP reporter gene.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that the BAC recombinant recapitulates endogenous expression

claim: Kaede fluorescent protein stably converts from green to red after exposure to UV light.
source: Kaede fluorescent protein (FPbase ID: Q31FH) stably converts from green to red after exposure to UV light (Ando et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Translated Kaede protein is detectable above background for at least 7 days in P. miniata embryos and larvae when grown at 15°C.
source: We experimentally measured the stability of Kaede, by injecting in vitro synthesized kaede mRNA into zygotes and quantifying fluorescence over time. We show that translated Kaede protein is detectable above background for at least 7 days in P. miniata embryos and larvae when grown at 15°C (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: GFP is extremely stable in P. miniata embryos, likely because they are grown at low temperatures.
source: This supports previous work which shows that GFP is extremely stable in these embryos, likely because they are grown at low temperatures (Arnone et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: At 2dpb and 3dpb, green-only, red-only, as well as yellow (green plus red) cells are observed in regenerating larvae injected with sox4:Kaede BAC.
source: At 2dpb and 3dpb we observe green-only, red-only, as well as yellow (green plus red) cells (Figure 3B and D–d).
evidence: Supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3B and D-d

claim: Red cells in the regenerating larvae are historically labeled cells that have expressed sox4 at some point prior to bisection but no longer express sox4.
source: Red cells in the regenerating larvae are the historically labeled cells that have expressed sox4 at some point prior to bisection but no longer express sox4. For example, these may have been differentiated neurons that no longer express the progenitor marker sox4.
evidence: Inference based on the properties of the photoconvertible Kaede reporter system

claim: Yellow cells are from existing larval and regenerative sox4+ cell lineages that expressed sox4 in the intact larvae and continue to express sox4 in their progeny after wounding.
source: The yellow cells are from existing larval and regenerative sox4+ cell lineages. That is, these cells expressed sox4 in the intact larvae and continue to express sox4 in their progeny after wounding.
evidence: Inference based on the properties of the photoconvertible Kaede reporter system

claim: Green-only cells are cells that have not previously expressed sox4 but are induced to start expressing sox4 only upon decapitation.
source: Most interestingly, there are green-only cells. These are cells that have not previously expressed sox4 but are induced to start expressing sox4 only upon decapitation.
evidence: Inference based on the properties of the photoconvertible Kaede reporter system

claim: There are high numbers of green+ sox4 cells in larvae photoconverted at 2dpf and examined at 5dpf.
source: We find that there are high numbers of green+ cells in larvae photoconverted at 2dpf (Figure 4B–C)
evidence: Supported by quantitative data from live imaging shown in Figure 4B-C

claim: There are almost no green+ sox4 cells in larvae photoconverted at 4dpf and examined at 7dpf.
source: but almost none in larvae converted at 4dpf (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data from live imaging shown in Figure 4D-E

claim: New sox4+ cells are actively being specified in embryos, but this specification has stopped by 4dpf (larval stage).
source: This is evidence that new sox4+ cells are actively being specified in embryos, but that this specification has stopped by 4dpf (i.e. larval stage).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the quantitative comparison of green sox4+ cells between embryonic and larval stages

claim: Specification of new sox4+ cells is highest in embryos, ends by late embryogenesis, and resumes in response to bisection induced regeneration.
source: Comparing the numbers of green (newly expressing) sox4+ cells during normal development with those counted in regeneration, we see that specification of new sox4+ cells is highest in embryos, ends by late embryogenesis, and resumes in response to bisection induced regeneration (Figure 4F, and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantitative comparison shown in Figure 4F

claim: Decapitation induces a wound response that re-initiates the specification of new sox4+ cells, a process which had stopped by day four of embryogenesis.
source: Thus, decapitation induces a wound response that re-initiates the specification of new sox4+ cells, a process which had stopped by day four of embryogenesis.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the quantitative comparison of sox4+ cell specification across development and regeneration

claim: Sox2 is expressed throughout the ectoderm in embryos and therefore broadly marks this germ layer.
source: During normal embryogenesis, the neural precursor cells are derived from sox2+ ectoderm. Sox2 is expressed throughout the ectoderm in embryos and therefore broadly marks this germ layer (Yankura et al., 2013; Yankura et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The sox2:Kaede BAC recombinant recapitulates the embryonic sox2 expression pattern.
source: After BAC injection, zygotes started to express Kaede at 24-48hpf in broad patches of ectodermal cells. By larval stage, Kaede was detected on the ectoderm including the ciliary bands, dorsal ganglia, and ectodermally derived neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C'). This localization pattern recapitulates the embryonic sox2 expression pattern reported previously (Yankura et al., 2013; Yankura et al., 2010; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by comparison of BAC expression pattern with previously published sox2 expression data

claim: Sox4+ cells overlap completely with sox2+ cells on the ectoderm in normally developing larvae.
source: When we examine expression in normal developing larvae, we find that sox4+ cells overlap completely with sox2+ cells on the ectoderm as is expected in normally developing larvae (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-D''), although not all sox2+ cells are sox4+, as sox2+ also produce non neural ectoderm.
evidence: Supported by double BAC labeling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-D''

claim: New (green+ cells) expression of sox2 is found following bisection, indicating that cells that had not previously expressed sox2 are now expressing the sox2 gene.
source: Strikingly, we found new (green+ cells) expression of sox2, indicating that cell that had not previously expressed sox2 are now expressing the sox2 gene following bisection.
evidence: Supported by live imaging data from photoconverted sox2:Kaede larvae

claim: Four of 15 observed larvae exhibited cells with colocalized green Kaede (new sox2 expression) and Cardinal (sox4) at the regenerating leading edge at 3dpb.
source: Furthermore, four of 15 observed larvae exhibited cells with colocalized green Kaede (new sox2 expression) and Cardinal (sox4,far red, pseudo-colored blue) at the regenerating leading edge (Figure 5 B(b-b3))at 3dpb.
evidence: Supported by quantitative data from double BAC labeling shown in Figure 5B(b-b3)

claim: New sox2+ cells start to express sox4 and thereby enter into neurogenesis pathways.
source: As the green Kaede reporter labels de novo sox2 expression, this shows that these new sox2+ cells start to express sox4 and thereby enter into neurogenesis pathways.
evidence: Inference based on the colocalization of green Kaede and Cardinal in the same cells

claim: At the time of bisection, all labeled sox4+ cells overlapped with sox2+ lineage in the imaged larvae.
source: However, it is important to note that at the time of bisection, all labeled sox4+ cells overlapped with sox2+ lineage in the imaged larvae. In other words, all Cardinal + cells are also red Kaede+ at the time of photoconversion.
evidence: Observation from the double BAC labeling experiment

claim: Cells derived from non sox2+ lineages are induced to express sox2 in regenerating larvae and will contribute to neural progenitors.
source: Thus, the sox4:Cardinal in Figure 5B must be expressed after wounding. This therefore supports the hypothesis that cells derived from non sox2+ lineages are induced to express sox2 in regenerating larvae and will contribute to neural progenitors.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that green Kaede+ Cardinal+ cells are present after wounding

claim: Sox2+ cells followed through to 7dpb show fluorescence in neural projections characteristic of fully formed neurons.
source: Indeed when we follow these larvae through to 7dpb (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-B) we find fluorescence in the neural projections which are characteristic of fully formed neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a1-a3).
evidence: Supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-B

claim: Newly specified sox2+ cells contributed to only tissues normally derived from sox2+ lineages in all regenerating larvae examined.
source: We examined at least 10 larvae over three independent injection batches and found that in all regenerating larvae the newly expressing sox2+ cells contributed to only tissues normally derived from sox2+ lineages (e.g. Figure 5—figure supplement 1E-F'').
evidence: Supported by quantitative observation across multiple larvae shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E-F''

claim: Sox2:Kaede green cells are observed in the outer ectodermal epithelium, the mouth, and ciliary bands.
source: We observed sox2:Kaede green cells in the outer ectodermal epithelium, the mouth, and ciliary bands.
evidence: Supported by observation from live imaging of sox2:Kaede larvae

claim: Once induced, sox2+ cells maintain their normal, embryonic fate potential.
source: This indicates that once induced these cells will maintain their normal, embryonic fate potential.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the observation that newly expressing sox2+ cells only contribute to normal sox2+ lineages

claim: Not all sox2+ cells enter the neurogenesis pathway in regeneration.
source: It is worth noting that not all sox2+ cells enter the neurogenesis pathway in regeneration (Figure 5 C(c1-c3)).
evidence: Supported by observation from double BAC labeling shown in Figure 5C(c1-c3)

claim: While larval sox2 cell lineages are restricted to ectodermal potency, they do not necessarily contribute only sox4+ neural fates.
source: This suggests that while larval sox2 cell lineages are restricted to ectodermal potency, they do not necessarily contribute only sox4+ neural fates.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that some sox2+ cells do not express sox4

claim: 25 µM of Aphidicolin is the minimum concentration needed to reliably inhibit cell division as assayed by EdU staining.
source: We first used a serial dilution test to determine that the 25 µM of Aphidicolin was the minimum concentration needed to reliably inhibit cell division as assayed by EdU staining, while cells in DMSO controls divided normally (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B

claim: Aphidicolin consistently blocked cell division over one week when applied with daily changes.
source: We incubated regenerated larvae in the drug or vehicle for up to 1 week, with daily changes into fresh drug or vehicle, and analyzed them every 24 hr to test that Aphidicolin consistently blocked cell division over this time (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: There are multiple yellow and green cells along the leading regenerated edge in aphidicolin-treated larvae at 3dpb.
source: We then assayed for red, green, or yellow-positive cells (Figure 6C–D", and Figure 6—source data 1). We show that there are multiple yellow, green cells along the leading regenerated edge.
evidence: Supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 6C-D'' and quantitative data in Figure 6—source data 1

claim: Cells which were not previously expressing sox2 are able to initiate expression of this gene in the absence of cell division and are thus not the result of asymmetric stem cell division.
source: This confirms that cells which were not previously expressing sox2 are now able to initiate expression of this gene in the absence of cell division and are thus not the result of asymmetric stem cell division.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the observation of green sox2+ cells in aphidicolin-treated larvae

claim: Echinoderms have an impressive ability for extensive whole body regeneration found in most species of the phylum.
source: Echinoderms on the other hand have an impressive ability for extensive whole body regeneration found in most species of the phylum (Ferrario et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to review literature

claim: The emerging consensus from echinoderm regeneration studies is that echinoderms rely extensively on wound-adjacent dedifferentiation for regenerating lost tissues.
source: The emerging consensus from these and other studies is that echinoderms rely extensively on wound-adjacent dedifferentiation for regenerating lost tissues (Ferrario et al., 2020; Mashanov and Zueva, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to review literature

claim: Expression of stem-cell marker genes have been identified as possible cell sources in some echinoderm species.
source: Conversely, expression of stem-cell marker genes have been identified as possible cell sources in some species (Mashanov et al., 2015b; Reinardy et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: There are many parallels between echinoderm larval development and early vertebrate development, particularly in the formation of the anterior-posterior axis and development of the nervous system.
source: Although pentaradial as adults, there are many parallels between echinoderm larval development and early vertebrate development, particularly in the formation of the anterior-posterior axis and development of the nervous system (Angerer et al., 2011; Hinman and Burke, 2018; Range et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: When sea star larvae are decapitated, they are able to regenerate their anterior structures.
source: Previous work has shown that when these sea star larvae are decapitated, they are able to regenerate their anterior structures (Cary et al., 2019b; Oulhen et al., 2016; Vickery et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: Sox4+ cells are scattered throughout the ectoderm where they function as precursors for multiple neural types in P. miniata larvae.
source: In embryos, sox2 is expressed throughout the ectoderm, while sox4+ cells are scattered throughout the ectoderm where they function as precursors for multiple neural types in the larvae (Cheatle Jarvela et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Lhx2 is needed for the differentiation of serotonergic neurons in P. miniata embryos.
source: We have also previously shown that lhx2 is needed for the differentiation of serotonergic neurons (Cheatle Jarvela et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Ectodermal elav expression is a marker of differentiated neurons in P. miniata.
source: We have previously demonstrated that these gene products mark the embryonic neurogenesis pathways, and that ectodermal elav expression is a marker of differentiated neurons (Cheatle Jarvela et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: The human and mouse orthologs of the sea star sox2 gene have well-characterized functions in the induction of pluripotency and maintenance of stem cells, especially neurogenic stem cells.
source: The human and mouse orthologs of the sea star sox2 gene have well-characterized functions in the induction of pluripotency and maintenance of stem cells, especially neurogenic stem cells (Feng and Wen, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: In combination with Oct4, Klf4, and c-Myc, sox2 can reprogram human and mouse somatic cells to pluripotent states.
source: In combination with Oct4, Klf4, and c-Myc, sox2 can reprogram human and mouse somatic cells to pluripotent states (Soufi et al., 2015; Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Other models of echinoderm regeneration have implicated, although not demonstrated, a role for orthologs of pluripotency factors in de-differentiation.
source: Other models of echinoderm regeneration have implicated, although not demonstrated, a role for orthologs of these pluripotency factors in de-differentiation (Mashanov and Zueva, 2019; Mashanov et al., 2015a).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: Klf4 is expressed at the wound edge following bisection and is presumably co-localized with sox2.
source: We have also previously shown that Klf4 is expressed at the wound edge following bisection and is thus presumably co-localized with sox2 (Cary et al., 2019b).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work and inference about colocalization

claim: Once respecified, sox2+ cells are restricted to become ectoderm, and the lip of mouth ectoderm/endoderm cell types, indicating that they are multi-potent but germline restricted.
source: We have shown that once respecified, sox2+ cells are restricted to become ectoderm, and the lip of mouth ectoderm/endoderm cell types, indicating that they are multi-potent but germline restricted.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the lineage tracing data showing sox2+ cells only contribute to ectodermal lineages

claim: In embryos, sox2+ cells are restricted to ectodermal lineages and the lip of the mouth.
source: In embryos, sox2+ cells are also restricted to ectodermal lineages and the lip of the mouth
evidence: Supported by previous knowledge of embryonic sox2 expression and lineage

claim: The wound-induced sox2+ cells enter their normal, embryonic lineage.
source: and therefore, the wound-induced sox2+ cells now enter their normal, embryonic lineage.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparison of regenerative and embryonic sox2+ cell lineages

claim: A subset of induced sox2+ cells recapitulate an embryonic neurogenesis pathway to reform serotonergic neurons around the mouth, and the latero-dorsal ganglia.
source: A subset of these induced cells recapitulate an embryonic neurogenesis pathway to reform serotonergic neurons around the mouth, and the latero-dorsal ganglia.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the lineage tracing and gene expression data

claim: The freshwater planarian, Schmidtea mediterranea, utilizes a population of heterogeneous pluripotent somatic stem cells, called neoblasts, to proliferate and differentiate to replace body parts.
source: For example, the freshwater planarian, Schmidtea mediterranea, utilizes a population of heterogeneous pluripotent somatic stem cells, called neoblasts, to proliferate and differentiate to replace body parts (Sánchez Alvarado, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Specialized neoblasts can divide to produce neoblasts that are pluripotent, suggesting a plasticity of their fate.
source: Recent work shows that specialized neoblasts can also divide to produce neoblasts that are pluripotent, suggesting a plasticity of their fate (Raz et al., 2021)
evidence: Supported by citation to recent work

claim: Species such as Hydra and axolotl refate differentiated cells either through dedifferentiation or transdifferentiation.
source: Species such as Hydra and axolotl, refate differentiated cells either through dedifferentiation or transdifferentiation (Gerber et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Hydra also utilizes interstitial cells as a population of stem cells.
source: Although, Hydra also utilizes interstitial cells as a population of stem cells (Siebert et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Cellular plasticity varies widely, from the totipotent planarian neoblasts to lineage restricted progenitors used by vertebrate animals.
source: Cellular plasticity also varies widely, from the totipotent planarian neoblasts to lineage restricted progenitors used by vertebrate animals (Kragl et al., 2009; Zhu and Pearson, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Echinoderm larvae induce non-stem cells into ectodermal neural stem cells, possibly through dedifferentiation or other mechanisms of fate conversion.
source: Our data indicate that echinoderm larvae induce non-stem cells into ectodermal neural stem cells, possibly through dedifferentiation or other mechanisms of fate conversion, as we see de novo sox2+ cells becoming neurons in regenerating larvae.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the lineage tracing data showing de novo sox2+ cells contribute to neurons

claim: There is a maintained lineage of sox2+ and sox4+ progenitors in bisected larvae that reform the nervous system.
source: Additionally, we show that there is a maintained lineage of sox2+ and sox4+ progenitors in bisected larvae, also reforming the nervous system, as we see yellow neurons in regenerating larvae (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data showing yellow neurons in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A

claim: Echinoderms may have a natural capacity to maintain a cellular plasticity that permits induction of new lineage stem-cells, as well as an ability to use existing lineage-restricted stem cells.
source: We posit that echinoderms may have a natural capacity to maintain a cellular plasticity that permits induction of new lineage stem-cells, as well as an ability to use existing lineage-restricted stem cells and that this flexibility may underlie their extensive abilities for regeneration.
evidence: Speculative conclusion drawn from the combined observations of de novo sox2+ cell induction and maintained sox2+/sox4+ lineages

claim: The BAC DNA construct is stably inherited by clones of cells and therefore present mosaically in the cells of the larvae.
source: The BAC DNA construct is stably inherited by clones of cells and therefore present mosaically in the cells of the larvae.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of BAC transgenesis in echinoderms

claim: Multiple constructs when co-injected into echinoderm zygotes are co-integrated, and are therefore inherited in the same cellular lineages.
source: It is important to note that multiple constructs when co-injected into echinoderm zygotes are then co-integrated, and are therefore inherited in the same cellular lineages (Cheatle Jarvela et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Aphidicolin is a conserved inhibitor of cell division that is particularly well characterized in echinoderms where it is known to block DNA polymerase function, nuclear break down and microtubule organizing centers.
source: We bathed sea star larvae in Aphidicolin, a conserved inhibitor of cell division, that is particularly well characterized in echinoderms where it is known to block DNA polymerase function, nuclear break down and microtubule organizing centers (Mashanov et al., 2017; Nishioka et al., 1984).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Reestablishing axial patterning is a commonly observed early feature in many species undergoing whole body regeneration.
source: Reestablishing axial patterning is a commonly observed early feature in many species undergoing whole body regeneration (Gehrke et al., 2019; Reddien, 2019), which we now show also occurs in sea star larvae.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The vertebrates, with some few exceptions, have limited capacity for regeneration that is usually restricted to specific cells, tissues and organs.
source: The vertebrates, with some few exceptions, have limited capacity for regeneration that is usually restricted to specific cells, tissues and organs (Rodriguez and Kang, 2020; Tanaka and Reddien, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to review literature

claim: The emerging evidence in vertebrates points to the use of tissue-specific stem cells and corresponding specific niches as a cellular source for regeneration.
source: The emerging evidence points to the use of tissue-specific stem cells and corresponding specific niches as a cellular source for regeneration (Kragl et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Molecular and ultrastructural studies in brittle star arm regeneration point to use of adjacent epithelial cells to differentiate into sclerocytes needed for arm skeleton regeneration, recapitulating, at least in part, a development program.
source: For example, molecular and ultrastructural studies in brittle star arm regeneration point to use of adjacent epithelial cells to differentiate into sclerocytes needed for arm skeleton regeneration, recapitulating, at least in part, a development program (Piovani et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Comprehensive studies in the regeneration of radial nerve chords in sea cucumbers point to the use of radial glial dedifferentiation in nervous system regeneration.
source: Comprehensive studies in the regeneration of radial nerve chords in sea cucumbers also point to the use of radial glial dedifferentiation in nervous system regeneration (Mashanov and Zueva, 2019; Mashanov et al., 2015a).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: It has been well documented that echinoderm larval forms are capable of extensive regeneration.
source: It has now been well documented that the larval forms are also capable of extensive regeneration (Oulhen et al., 2016; Vickery et al., 2001; Kasahara et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Sea stars have extensive regenerative capacities, a feature which extends across both their adult and larval life phases.
source: Sea stars, as typical for echinoderms, have extensive regenerative capacities, a feature which extends across both their adult and larval life phases (Vickery et al., 2001; Vickery et al., 2002; Ben Khadra et al., 2017; Hernroth et al., 2010; Oulhen et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The serotonergic postmitotic neuronal number is stable in larvae from day 4 or 5 of development.
source: The subsidence of sox4+ cell formation in the larval stage is consistent with data showing that the serotonergic postmitotic neuronal number is stable in larvae from day 4 or 5 of development (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: Cell division occurs throughout the normal larva, but then decreases in the early bisected larva and is then predominantly localized to the wound adjacent anterior at 3dpb.
source: We have previously shown that cell division occurs throughout the normal larva, but then decreases in the early bisected larva and is then predominantly localized to the wound adjacent anterior at 3dpb (Cary et al., 2019b).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work
